heroHeadline: Diplomatic Standoff: UK Envoy Flags Kunar Civilian Casualties; Pakistan Rejects Remarks; UN Alarms on Afghan Deportations
heroSubtitle: The Af-Pak conflict entered a diplomatic escalation phase May 1–3 as UK Special Envoy Richard Lindsay publicly called for an end to Durand Line violence following the April 28 Asadabad university strike and April 30 barrage of 200+ missiles on Kunar. Pakistan's Foreign Office fired back on May 2, calling the UK remarks 'one-sided' and claiming 52 Pakistani civilians killed and 84 injured by cross-border Afghan attacks since the conflict began — figures sharply contested by the Afghan Taliban, which documented 411+ Afghan civilian deaths and hundreds of wounded from Pakistani strikes. The UN formally raised alarm on May 3 over Pakistan's accelerating forced deportations of Afghan refugees, with 146,000+ expelled in 2026 and over 280,000 deported from Pakistan and Iran combined in April alone. The Urumqi Round 2 peace talks, expected by end-April, have not taken place. China has maintained silence on specific Pakistani strike incidents. No ceasefire is in force.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNAMA, SIGAR, ACLED, Brown University Costs of War Project, US DoD, Reuters, BBC, Tolo News, Dawn, Al Jazeera, HRW, OHCHR, OCHA
